svg.title: TYPE_REPARK_TRAY / TYPE_MOVE_TRAY -> ExpandReparkTrayJob()
svg.desc: Move one tray to a parking node. Two jobs move the same tray, so rule A chains them. Six other job methods create their tray moves through this method.
svg.metadata: ["Start: the request arrives. The map is working_state as the method first sees it; no events yet. Step through the method one table row at a time.", "Row 1. A repark needs at least a tray or a destination; with neither there is nothing to plan. In this example: Both are given. (passes)", "Row 2. Make a scratch copy of the request's garage and apply every event already in the DAG, so the method sees the garage as earlier jobs will leave it. A replay that fails fails the job. In this example: Job 1 replays event 1, so working_state has T19 at P24. (replay)", "Row 3. Look the tray up in the scratch garage, so a tray an earlier job moved is seen where that move leaves it. Unknown or disabled trays are rejected. In this example: Job 0 reads T19 at P19; job 1 reads it at P24, where job 0 leaves it. The initial_state fallback is only for a tray that an earlier move without a destination took out of the planned state. (passes)", "Row 4. A tray on a VECS that is charging must stop charging first; the stop is chained after the VECS's previous event. Any other non-ready VECS state fails the job. In this example: P19 has no VECS. (skipped)", "Row 5. Choose the parking heading on a plain parking node: a loaded tray faces the node's retrieval heading so a later retrieve is fast; an empty tray keeps its heading if that fits. In this example: Job 0: P24 is parking and T19 carries a car, so the heading becomes P24's retrieval heading. Job 1 has allow_reciprocal = false. (heading set)", "Row 6. If the tray is already at the destination pose, succeed without a move. In this example: Job 0: P19 against P24; job 1: P24 against P23. Neither job is a no-op. (no early exit)", "Row 7. A loaded tray takes the destination node's retrieval heading, if the node has one, whatever the node type. In this example: T19 is loaded, so the retrieval heading of P24 (job 0) or P23 (job 1) is used if that node has one. (dest set)", "Row 8. Reject destinations that are a VECS not ready to charge, not in the graph, kept out for this tray, or a disabled bay. In this example: P24 and P23 are plain, enabled parking. (passes)", "Row 9. Create the TrayMove, add it to the DAG and chain it after this tray's previous event (rule A). In this example: Job 0: T19 has no earlier event. Job 1: T19's last event is 1, so edge 1 -> 2. (adds 1, 2 \u00b7 A)", "Row 10. If the destination is a bay or VECS, also wait for that resource's last event (rule C). In this example: Neither destination is a bay or VECS. (rule C skipped)", "Row 11. Make the move wait for earlier events of the same job (rule B). In this example: Each job has one event: no rule B edge. (no edge)", "Playing the plan (one illustrative execution: AGV assignment and motion planning choose the real AGV and route): AGV-1 drives empty W26 -> P23 -> P19 and stops under T19 (the approach for event 1; AGV assignment adds such moves later).", "Playing the plan: event 1. AGV-1 lifts T19, carries it P19 -> P23 -> P24 and lowers it.", "Playing the plan: event 2. AGV-1 lifts T19, carries it P24 -> P23 and lowers it. No approach drive: AGV-1 is still under T19 after event 1. Every tray and AGV is now where the plan leaves it."]
